. In animal models 
inflammatory disease does not occur in the absence of gut micro-
biota. Normally, when an antigenic challenge or trauma occurs, 
the immune response is initiated; it is then turned off and con-
tinues to be held in check after the challenge resolves. In IBD 
however, increased antigen exposure, decreased host defense 
mechanisms, and/or decreased tolerance to some components of 
the gut microbiota occurs. Inappropriate inflammatory response 
and an inability to suppress it play primary roles in the disease.
